newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart raises dividend, expands stock buy back.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart raises dividend, expands stock buy back.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc. said Thursday that it raised its dividend by 29 percent and that it expanded its share buy back programme fivefold to $2 billion worth of stock over the next 12 to 18 months.

The Bentonville, Ark.-based company had previously announced a $400 million stock buy back programme in the third quarter of last year. The shares to be repurchased are expected to represent less than 4 percent of the company's currently outstanding shares.
The nation's largest retailer said it raised its quartlery dividend to 67.5 cents from 52.5 cents per share.

"The significant increase in both the dividend and share repurchase demonstrate our strong confidence in the Company's future earnings and cash flow growth," said Wal-Mart Chief Executive Officer David Glass.
The quarterly dividend is payable April 9 to shareholders of record on March 19.
Wal-Mart stock rose 37.5 cents to $27 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
